newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar still weak in solid turnover.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar still weak in solid turnover.

text.p: Follow-through selling of London's August white sugar contract dragged other nearby prices lower on Thursday in line with the raws market but bargain hunters moved in at the lows, traders said.

Although London was mostly weaker in the morning, a bout of selling by fund players in New York, then joined by locals, pushed July raws down from its peak of 11.21 cents/lb, prompting further selling in London.
Outright trade dealings dominated activity in London and while interest was noted in August/October, there was increasing volume on the back spreads, traders said.
"It's been fairly mixed but the trade are quite prominent on both sides," said one, noting the healthy London volume despite the absence of many major players.
At 1555 GMT August was down $1.30 at $320.10 after an intraday high of $322.00.

Mixed August buying on Wednesday, helped later by firmer sentiment on July raws, drove the spot price through initial resistance and up to a high of $321.50, already surpassed by 50 cents on Thursday.

But traders said the reasons for the rally were unclear as physical activity had been quiet recently and there had been no confirmation of rumoured Russian purchases, a major talking point over the last week.
October was 30 cents down at $311.00 and volume was a solid 2,276 lots, more than half of which was in August.

Trading was thin on the Paris market with just 228 lots on the board. August was down $1.30 at $320.00, leaving the arbitrage against London at a tight nominal value of 10 cents. October was up 60 cents at $312.10.
